name: Wealth Management
description: Advisory and discretionary investment services, financial planning, and private banking for high-net-worth individuals

sub_capabilities.name: Investment Advisory
sub_capabilities.description: Regulated investment advice, suitability assessments, and product recommendations for wealth clients

distinct_participants.rationale: Participants are wealth clients and relationship managers — shared across all wealth sub-capabilities

distinct_regulatory_framework.rationale: Governed by MiFID II suitability rules (Article 25) and FCA COBS 9A, the same framework applicable to Portfolio Management and Financial Planning

distinct_lifecycle.rationale: Lifecycle is tightly coupled to the advisory relationship and feeds directly into Portfolio Management; not independently bounded

independent_scalability.rationale: Volume scales with the overall wealth client book, not independently of other wealth sub-capabilities

sub_capabilities.name: Portfolio Management
sub_capabilities.description: Discretionary portfolio management, asset allocation, rebalancing, and performance reporting for wealth clients

distinct_participants.rationale: Participants are the same wealth clients and portfolio managers that interact across all wealth sub-capabilities

distinct_regulatory_framework.rationale: Governed by MiFID II Articles 24–25 and FCA COBS 6/9A, the same framework shared with Investment Advisory and Financial Planning

distinct_lifecycle.rationale: Lifecycle is bound to the client investment mandate, which originates in Investment Advisory and is closed in Financial Planning reviews; not independently bounded

independent_scalability.rationale: AUM growth is correlated with the wealth client book across all sub-capabilities; no independent scaling driver

sub_capabilities.name: Private Banking
sub_capabilities.description: Dedicated relationship management, bespoke lending facilities, and concierge services for high-net-worth clients

distinct_participants.rationale: Private banking clients are a subset of wealth clients; relationship managers serve across private banking and advisory services

distinct_regulatory_framework.rationale: Lending components fall under FSMA 2000 and FCA MCOB; advisory components remain under MiFID II/FCA COBS — the blended framework is shared with other wealth sub-capabilities rather than being uniquely distinct

distinct_lifecycle.rationale: Client onboarding, relationship management, and offboarding are shared lifecycle stages with Investment Advisory and Portfolio Management

independent_scalability.rationale: Private banking capacity scales with the relationship manager headcount that is shared across the wealth management capability

sub_capabilities.name: Financial Planning
sub_capabilities.description: Retirement planning, tax-efficient investment structuring, and estate planning for wealth clients

distinct_participants.rationale: Financial planning clients are the same wealth client population; planners operate within the same relationship model as advisers and portfolio managers

distinct_regulatory_framework.rationale: Governed by MiFID II, FCA COBS 9, and FCA PROD — the same framework covering the full wealth management capability

distinct_lifecycle.rationale: Planning engagements are typically initiated and reviewed as part of the broader investment advisory and portfolio management lifecycle

independent_scalability.rationale: Demand scales with the wealth client book; no distinct volume driver that would justify independent capability scaling

design_decisions.title: All wealth sub-capabilities retained within CAP-006
design_decisions.decision: Investment Advisory, Portfolio Management, Private Banking, and Financial Planning are retained as sub-capabilities of CAP-006 rather than promoted to standalone capabilities.
design_decisions.rationale: All four sub-capabilities fail every promotion criterion: (1) Participants — they share the same high-net-worth client population and wealth relationship manager workforce; (2) Regulatory framework — all are governed by the same MiFID II / FCA COBS / FCA PROD regime with no sub-capability facing a materially separate regulatory body or rulebook; (3) Lifecycle — onboarding, ongoing relationship management, and offboarding are shared lifecycle stages with no cleanly independent boundaries; (4) Independent scalability — capacity and demand scale uniformly with the overall wealth client book. Promotion would introduce artificial domain boundaries, duplicate governance structures, and increase coordination overhead without architectural benefit.

design_decisions.title: MiFID II suitability obligation sits at capability level, not sub-capability level
design_decisions.decision: MiFID II Article 25 suitability and appropriateness obligations are treated as a capability-level cross-cutting concern rather than being assigned to Investment Advisory alone.
design_decisions.rationale: Suitability assessments inform product recommendations (Investment Advisory), asset allocation decisions (Portfolio Management), and planning recommendations (Financial Planning). Scoping the obligation to a single sub-capability would create compliance gaps and require duplication of assessment logic. A single capability-level suitability framework covers all sub-capabilities consistently and aligns with FCA COBS 9A expectations for integrated wealth services.
